name: T-Beauty

lead: T-Beauty is the label for Thai beauty brands and trends, which blend Thai spa and herbal traditions with modern formulation. For looks, it offers lightweight sunscreens, acne-focused skincare and hybrid makeup designed for heat and humidity.
Its rise is documented mostly in trade and press coverage; academic work on Thai beauty touches on preferred nasal profiles and facial proportions among Thai people.

paras: Users adopt Thai skincare and makeup products, including sweat-resistant and tinted sunscreens and acne products with ingredients such as niacinamide, salicylic acid, centella asiatica or turmeric.
Beauty products carry the usual risks of irritation or allergy. Thailand regulates cosmetics by product notification rather than pre-market approval.

angle.text: Products target acne, sun protection and wearable makeup in hot climates. Users pick them for price and fit to local conditions.

lead: T-Beauty, or Thai beauty, is the label for Thai cosmetic and skincare brands and aesthetic trends. A trade article describes it as combining Thailand's spa and herbal traditions with modern formulation, built for heat, humidity and UV exposure.[1]

For appearance, the pitch is lightweight, sweat-resistant sunscreens including tinted SPF, multifunctional skincare and hybrid makeup. Commonly cited ingredients include niacinamide, salicylic acid, turmeric, centella asiatica and mangosteen. Brands named include Ingu Skin, Mistine, Panpuri and Cathy Doll.[1]

The same source cites projections that Thailand's beauty market would exceed US$7.1 billion by end-2025, with skincare about half of value, and acne the top skin concern for younger consumers.[1] Research on Thai aesthetics includes a 2024 survey of preferred nasal profiles and a 2025 preprint on facial proportions among Thailand's three major ethnic groups.[2][3]
infobox: Ingu Skin, Mistine, Panpuri, Cathy Doll

paras: T-Beauty combines spa and herbal heritage with modern science. Product types include sunscreens, sticks, mists, gels and powders, plus multifunctional skincare.[1]

Nearly half of Thai beauty purchases are made online, and searches for salicylic acid on Thai e-commerce platforms rose over 65% and centella asiatica 48%, per Mintel data cited by the trade article.[1] Mistine's sunscreens are described as bestsellers on China's Tmall.[1]

A cross-sectional study of Thai adults aged 18-60 examined preferred nasal profiles and rhinoplasty awareness.[2] A 2025 preprint analysed facial proportions of 131 Thai women from Thai-Indian, Thai-Thai and Thai-Chinese backgrounds to build a balanced facial model.[3]
No studies found on T-Beauty products as a category. Related research examines Thai facial aesthetics.[2][3]
